verdicts.trueWording: editorial relationship for the majority of my career
verdicts.note: Fuller Award program PDF fetched raw and pdftotext-extracted; Hartwell tribute (p.17-18 of the tributes section). Sentence names Aldiss, Heinlein, Herbert, Dick, then singles Wolfe out as the longest editorial relationship of his career. Quote present word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: part of my reputation as an editor derives
verdicts.note: Same Hartwell tribute, sentence immediately following the one behind 649; it completes with the fact that he is Wolfe's editor. Verbatim on the raw PDF text.

verdicts.trueWording: what I was doing well (Dialogue! Character!)
verdicts.note: Ultan's Library page fetched raw. Paragraph beginning 'And after I sent my chapters, I received a letter' lists keen insight, encouragement, the parenthesis quoted, and 'most importantly, stuff I needed to work on' - the fault limb, expanded next sentence as her habit of interrupting dialogue with infodumps ('lumps of prose like uncooked dumplings'). Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: I can read it, but I can't promise to say anything
verdicts.note: Raw page, the dinner paragraph: she asks if he will read her novel, his face 'got very careful indeed', and he gently says the quoted line, which continues 'about it'. Both limbs - agreeing to read, refusing to promise comment - are on the page.

Raw page, late paragraph: 'I still overwrite my early drafts (Gene told me he does too)'. The overwriting-early-drafts limb is Cooney's own clause the parenthesis attaches to, so Wolfe's 'too' carries it.

verdicts.trueWording: Scrub her face. Give her a new dress.
verdicts.note: Raw page, closing section: prefaced by 'And when it's done... look at your story again' and followed by 'And send her back out into the world' - the finished-story limb and the sending-out-again limb both explicit.

Raw page, the cover-letters/submitting paragraph. The full sentence names writers who do not subscribe to the magazines they submit to, and Cooney adds 'He was clear on that point', supporting the rule framing.

verdicts.trueWording: Knight also brings him to the Milford Writer's Workshop
verdicts.note: The Ringer article fetched raw (article body recovered from the page HTML). The Orbit paragraph carries the quote in the present tense used throughout the piece, and three sentences later: 'Gene has never had writing peers before' - the first-time-peers limb.

verdicts.trueWording: the only person who helped me with my writing
verdicts.note: gwern.net raw HTML of the McCaffery interview; the answer to the Fifth Head dedication question. Full clause ends '...when I really needed help was Damon Knight'.

verdicts.trueWording: it needs to change here from viewpoint A to viewpoint B
verdicts.note: Same answer. Wolfe describes sending 'Trip Trap' to Orbit and getting it back with Knight's letter; the quoted clause is followed by '-and this is why-' and then a further switch from B to C, so the where-and-why limb holds. The letter was a rejection ('I got it back').

verdicts.trueWording: a long list of very sensible suggestions of that sort
verdicts.note: Same sentence as 661, its closing clause. 'Long' is on the page immediately before the quoted span.

verdicts.trueWording: on the bed for a long while, and I suddenly realized
verdicts.note: Same answer: 'After I read that letter I lay' precedes the quote, and the realisation is given as 'By golly, I'm actually a writer now.' All three limbs on the raw page.

verdicts.trueWording: I didn't know I had grown you from a bean
verdicts.note: Same answer: Wolfe says he wrote something like that to Damon and 'he wrote back' the quoted line, 'which is the line I stole for my dedication'. Knight's authorship and the writing-back limb both explicit; McCaffery's question quotes the dedication as 'who one night in 1966 grew me from a bean'.

verdicts.trueWording: there had been no re write
verdicts.note: Same answer, raw page (the interview text spells it 're write'). Galaxy rejected the story; he sent it to If, not knowing Pohl edited both; 'I got an acceptance from Pohl... with a check' and the letter praised the improvement. 'Resubmitted' is fair - Pohl saw the same story a second time, which is what his letter says.

verdicts.trueWording: I'm glad you let me see this again
verdicts.note: Same answer: 'His letter said,' introduces the quoted sentence, and the next sentence on the page is the rewrite-praise sentence the claim also quotes. Both sentences match word for word, including the spaced 're write'.
